title: How to Photograph Products Without a Camera (Just Your Phone) Like a Pro
description: No DSLR? No problem. Modern phone cameras + AI editing produce catalog-quality product photos. Here's the workflow.

blocks.text: The "you need a real camera" era is officially over. Modern phones (iPhone 12+, Samsung S22+, Pixel 6+) shoot product photos indistinguishable from DSLRs at typical browsing sizes.
Here's the phone-only workflow that competes with $2,000 setups.
Why Phones Actually Work Now
Modern phones have:
At 1200x1200 (Amazon size) or 1000x1500 (Pinterest size), phones are indistinguishable from professional cameras.
The Phone Setup

items.text: Manual exposure lock (tap product, hold to lock)
HEIC or RAW format if available

blocks.text: Five settings. Ten seconds to enable. Massive quality gain.
The Shooting Technique

items.text: Distance: 1-3 feet from product (avoid extreme close-up which distorts)
Height: Slightly above product, angled slightly down
Light: Behind you or 45° off-axis (never behind product unless intentional)
Stability: Use both hands or a $10 phone tripod

blocks.text: The AI Editing Bridge
Phone photos + AI editing = catalog quality.
Workflow:

items.text: Import to computer (or edit directly on phone)

blocks.text: Ten minutes per product. Zero equipment cost.
The Portrait Mode Warning
Portrait mode blurs backgrounds—which sounds great. But:

items.text: Amazon prohibits blurred backgrounds on main images
Some products need full sharpness end-to-end
Portrait mode edges are sometimes wonky

blocks.text: Better: Shoot in standard mode with a clean background, then remove background properly at edit-photo.com.
The Macro Mode Trick
For jewelry, cosmetics, small electronics—macro mode is a game changer. Details visible on phone macro rival $500+ macro lenses on DSLRs.
Shoot macro details separately as additional images.
The Lighting Reality
Best phone photography light: North-facing window between 10 AM and 2 PM.
Alternatives:
Never use direct flash. Ever. It's the amateur signal that instantly gives away phone photos.
The Common Phone Photo Mistakes
Zooming in digitally. Kills resolution. Move closer instead.
Tilted verticals. Straight walls and edges must be straight. Use grid overlay.
Overexposed whites. Blown-out backgrounds lose detail. Underexpose slightly, recover in editing.
Multiple photos in different lighting. Consistency requires shooting in one session.
The Full Phone-Only Catalog
For a 50-product catalog:

items.text: One weekend of shooting (a few hours)
One weekend of editing at edit-photo.com
Zero equipment cost beyond a $10 tripod

blocks.text: Result: A catalog that competes with sellers who spent $5,000 on gear.
The Rich Man's Objection
"But a DSLR is objectively better..."
Sure, at 100% zoom on a 27" monitor. At 300x300 pixels on a phone screen (where 80% of your buyers actually see your photos), a phone photo edited well is identical to a DSLR photo edited well.
Buy a camera when you're scaling to $100K+/month. Until then, phone + edit-photo.com wins on ROI.
Start Shooting with What You Have
Perfection kills action. Your phone is enough. Start free at edit-photo.com.
